Order:

1. Vide this order I am disposing application moved by the petitioner/victim under Section 408 of Cr.P.C. for transfer of the case from the court of Sh. Pawan Kumar, Ld. ASJ (SFTC), NDD, PHC to some other court of competent jurisdiction.

2. Respondents are facing trial in SC No.281/2019, FIR No.30/2019, Police Station Inderpuri,
U/s.323/376/506/509 IPC and the matter was fixed for framing of charge on 13.12.2023.
3. This case is pending for framing of charge since 22.07.2019.
Neither the prosecution has ever sought any permission by filing the charge or afterwards, despite that Ld. ASJ vide order dated 14.07.2022 has directed the IO to file certain documents on record.

Petitioner was initially represented by Ld. Counsel provided by the Legal Aid and he had put forth grievances of the petitioner before the Ld. ASJ stating that matter is pending for the last four years at the same stage.

It is thereby requested that the case be transferred to some other court.
4. Ld. Counsel for respondent Nos.1 & 2 has opted not to file reply to this petition.

5. Heard arguments of Sh. Ishan Jain, Ld. Counsel for the petitioner, Sh. Gautam Khazanchi and Sh.
Vaibhav Dubey, Ld.
Counsels for respondent Nos. 1 & 2 and have perused the record.
6. Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner, being victim, is getting further victimized because of the delay in the trial.
Moreover, she is being pressurized by the court to do settlement and hence, she has apprehension that she will not get justice in this court.
On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the respondents has stated that no such incident has happened as stated by the petitioner, the delay of two years has happened because of the pandemic.

It is stated that as alleged by the petitioner, the Ld. ASJ has never asked the petitioner to settle the dispute and to the reasons best known to the petitioner, she wants to get this case transferred from this court.
7. Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon para 7 of Chapter 26 of Delhi High Court Rules.

The relevant portion of which is as under :
"7. Common grounds on which applications for transfer are made--Applications for transfer of criminal cases are frequently made by accused persons on the allegation that such transfer is necessary in the interest of justice.

The most common grounds on which such applications for transfer are made are (a) that the Judge or Magistrate is personally interested in the case, or (b) that he is connected with one or the other party to the case by relationship,
friendship, etc., and is therefore, likely to be partial, or (c) that he has already formed or expressed an opinion on the subject matter of the enquiry or trial, or (d) that he has conducted himself in such a manner that no fair or impartial enquiry or trial can be expected from him".
8.
It is mentioned that this case is pending for framing of charge since 22.07.2019 i.e. for the last more than four years.
The charge-sheet was filed by the State (Respondent No.3) in the year 2019 and since then, the matter is at the stage of framing of charge.
It is further mentioned that no permission was sought by the prosecution either at the time of filing of the charge-sheet or thereafter to place on records certain documents.

However, Ld. ASJ vide order dated 14.07.2022 Smt. Runa Laxi vs Sh. Vijender Pal Singh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38685599/

10. Ld. Counsels for respondent Nos. 1 & 2 has relied upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Usmangani Adambhai Vahora Vs. State of Gujarat and Another: [(2016)
3 SCC 370], whereby the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under :
"7.So far as apprehension is concerned, it has to be one which would establish that justice will not be done.

entities.text:
Usmangani Adambhai Vahora Vs. State of Gujarat and Another: [(2016)
3 SCC 370]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this context, we may profitably refer to a passage from a three-judge Bench decision in Gurcharan Das Chadha Vs. State of Rajasthan, wherein it has been held: (AIR p.1423, para 13)".

entities.text: Gurcharan Das Chadha Vs. State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "13...The law with regard to transfer of cases is well-settled.
A case is transferred if there is a reasonable apprehension on the part of a party to a case that justice will not be done.
A petitioner is not required to demonstrate that justice will inevitably fail.
He is entitled to a transfer if he shows circumstances from which it can be inferred that he entertains an apprehension and that it is reasonable in the circumstances alleged.
It is one of the principles of the administration of justice that justice should not only be done but it should be seen to be done.
However, a mere allegation that there is apprehension that justice will not be done in a given case does not suffice.
The Court has further to see whether the apprehension is reasonable or not.
To judge of the reasonableness of the apprehension the state of the mind of the person who entertains the apprehension is no doubt relevant but that is not all.
The apprehension must not only be entertained but must appear to the Court to be a reasonable apprehension".

"8. This court in Abdul Nazar Madani Vs. State of T.N. has ruled that : (SCC pp.210-11,para 7)"

3 "7.....The apprehension of not getting a fair and impartial inquiry or trial is required to be reasonable and not imaginary, based upon conjectures and surmises.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If it appears that the dispensation of criminal justice is not possible impartially and objectively and without any bias, before any Court or even at any place, the appropriate Court may transfer the case to another Court where it feels that holding of fair and proper trial is conducive.
No universal or hard- and-fast rules can be prescribed for deciding a transfer petition which has always to be decided on the basis of the facts of each case.
Convenience of the parties including the witnesses to be produced at the trial is also a relevant consideration for deciding the transfer petition.
The convenience of the parties does not necessarily mean the convenience of the petitioners alone who approached the court on misconceived notions of apprehension.
Convenience for the purposes of transfer means the convenience of the prosecution, other accused, the witnesses and the larger interest of the society".

"9. In Amarinder Singh Vs. Prakash Singh Badal, while dealing with an application for transfer petition preferred under Section 406 Cr.P.C., a three-Judge Bench has opined that for transfer of a criminal case, there must be a reasonable apprehension on the part of the party to a case that justice will not be done.

entities.text: Amarinder Singh Vs. Prakash Singh Badal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has also been observed therein that merely an allegation that there is an apprehension that justice will not be done in a given case alone does not suffice.

It is also required on the part of the Court to see whether the apprehension alleged is reasonable or not, for the apprehension must not only be entertained but must appear to the Court to be a reasonable apprehension".
11.
Ld. Counsel for the respondent has placed on record copies of the up-to-date order sheets of this case.
Perused the order sheets.

As rightly stated by Ld. Counsel for the respondent, the delay in framing of the charge had taken place primarily because of the pandemic and further on account of the request made by the accused/respondent seeking summoning of the charge-sheet in FIR No.249/2018 PS Inderpuri.
12. For better appreciation of facts, comments of Ld. ASJ (SFTC), PHC, NDD were sought.

The Ld.
ASJ (SFTC) has filed his comments dated 03.02.2024.

Perused and considered the comments of Ld.
ASJ (SFTC).
13.
A litigant i.e. complainant or accused, is not allowed forum hunting.
Merely because an adverse order has been passed or delay has taken in disposal of the matter is not a ground to assume that the court is biased against one party.
The dictum of law is, "justice should not only be done but it should appears to have been done".
The petitioner is required to establish that there is reasonable apprehension that he may not get justice in this matter.

Here, one of the main apprehension shown by petitioner is on the premise that on 22.11.2023 in the absence of her counsel, the Ld. ASJ (SFTC)
directed the petitioner to settle the dispute with the accused and get free from the court proceedings.
The same stands denied by the Ld. ASJ (SFTC) in his comments.
It is beyond comprehension if any court in such a serious matter may ever ask the victim to settle the matter with the accused.
